newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks hit by profit-taking, low liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks hit by profit-taking, low liquidity.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed marginally higher but were held back by profit-taking and a lack of shares, brokers said.
The all share index closed up 1.01 points at 626.9. Turnover was 23.1 million rupees on 985,254 shares. Aitken Spence rose 1.25 rupees to 106.25, Kelani Valley one to 24.25.
"The expected profit-taking has set in," said Dimuthu Abeysekera, a trader at Allied Phillips Securities.
He added it would probably only slow down the advance of the index, and not reverse it since there was sufficient buying interest.
Brokers said trading was mainly supported by rich local investors taking long-term positions. Foreign investors were inactive and local institutions were stymied by a lack of shares, they added.

The stock exchange suspended trading of investment banks Vanik and Asia Capital, following a take-over bid by Asia Capital for Vanik. The offer price was based on eight rupees in cash and one new share of Asia Capital, for every Vanik share.
Asia Capital first made a takeover bid for Vanik in November 1996, based on the payment of 10 rupees in cash, and one new share, which was rejected by Vanik.
